chunks.text: The batch · June 7, twenty twenty-six · 4 min read · By Don Goldstein
Three hard dates inside the next six weeks and one cost spike across all of them. The June wave: four pieces on what changed, what to do, and the order to do it in.
Three DMV pressures stack in the next six weeks: DC's wage step on July 1 (18.40 dollars / 10.30 dollars tipped), the streatery program's end, and food costs (beef ~6.90 dollars/lb, FAFH +3.6%).
Four pieces, designed to be read in order: the wage deadline, the lost patio seats, the food re-cost, and the June calendar.
One muscle wins all four — margin math, a complete Google profile, and a clean reservation link.

Three pressures land on a DMV restaurant in the next six weeks, and they don’t politely take turns. July 1: DC’s minimum wage steps to 18.40 dollars and the tipped base to 10.30 dollars. This spring already: the temporary streateries are gone, with many operators down a chunk of patio seats just as summer peaks. And underneath both: ground beef at a record near 6.90 dollars a pound and food-away-from-home prices forecast up 3.6% across the year. None of them is the worst news on its own. Stacked, they ask one question — what do you do about it before they all show up in the August prime cost ?
This wave is four pieces, meant to be read in order, that walk that question. None of them ask for an ad budget; all of them pay you in margin.

The DMV reading ladder, four pieces in order. One: the DC wage step on July first — standard minimum to eighteen forty, tipped base to ten thirty, and the Initiative 82 framing correction most coverage still gets wrong. Two: the streatery loss — DDOT's twenty-dollar-per-square-foot road rent ended the curb-lane era; how to win the covers back. Three: food cost re-pricing — beef at six ninety and food-away-from-home up three point six percent; re-cost the five plates that moved, not the menu. Four: the June calendar — Father's Day, summer hiring, patio season; win the local search, not the price war.

Read together, the four point at a single muscle: the operator who knows their numbers and runs them on the same tools wins all four. The margin math that prices the July 1 wage step is the same math that prices the food-cost re-cost. The Google Business Profile that catches the diner who lost a streatery seat is the same profile that catches the Father’s Day booking. A clean reservation link is the single most-used asset across three of the four pieces.
Run the G B P grader and the margin math once, this week, and three of the four moves are already set up. The fourth — re-costing the plates that moved — needs a recipe-cost card per plate, no more.
Three deadlines. One June. Four pieces, in order — ready when you are.
The DC wage step is the hardest deadline; price for it before July 1, not after.
Streatery losses move covers indoors and online — the Google profile and the reservation link are the catch.
Do not raise the whole menu for the food spike; re-cost the three to five plates that actually moved.
June rewards the findable, bookable restaurant — not the cheapest one.
